sentence: Antibiotic and antiparasitic medicines, including metronidazole and tinidazole, that act on susceptible bacteria and parasites that live without oxygen.
Nitroimidazoles are switched on inside susceptible organisms by pathways that are absent in aerobic human cells.
The switched-on form produces short-lived products that bind to DNA and damage it.
In Giardia, enzymes such as pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase help to switch on 5-nitroimidazoles including metronidazole and tinidazole.
For metronidazole, the NHS advises avoiding alcohol during treatment and for 2 days afterwards.
Tinidazole is described as similar to metronidazole in its range of activity and side effects, so similar cautions may apply.
Feeling sick, diarrhoea and a metallic taste are the common side effects of metronidazole.
